condition: Atypical (lateral) anal ulcer — exclude Crohn’s, syphilis, HSV, TB, HIV-related ulcer and anal cancer
summary: 35-year-old man living with HIV (MSM) with a broad, indurated, relatively painless lateral anal ulcer and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Atypical fissure: EUA and biopsy, syphilis/HSV/TB testing, Crohn’s assessment. No sphincterotomy before a diagnosis.

inputs.hpi: Six weeks of a sore beside the anus with some discharge and spotting of blood, only mildly painful. HIV on antiretrovirals (last viral load undetectable, CD4 420). New partner 3 months ago. No bowel change, no weight loss.

exam.other: Perianal: 2 cm broad-based ulcer in the right lateral position with indurated, rolled edges, extending beyond the dentate line; no sentinel tag.

comorbidities: HIV infection (on ART, viral load undetectable)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Atypical lateral anal fissure/ulcer — cause to be established
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Atypical lateral anal ulcer with indurated edges and inguinal nodes in a man with HIV. Exclude syphilis, HSV, TB, Crohn’s and anal squamous cell carcinoma: EUA and biopsy, serology and swabs.

match: squamous cell carcinoma of the anus

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Syphilis/HSV/TB/Crohn’s are not in the PANE top 3 for an atypical fissure (the protocol red flag mentions them). | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 5 of ios.bayes: 1. Perianal Abscess | 2. Anal Carcinoma | 3. Inguinal Hernia | 4. Fournier's Gangrene | 5. Femoral Hernia

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add an "atypical fissure" dx-variant (lateral, multiple, painless, indurated, HIV/IBD) that replaces the treatment phases with EUA + biopsy, syphilis/HSV/HIV/TB testing and Crohn’s assessment (ASCRS 2023).

mustExclude.note: Sphincterotomy (or botulinum) for an undiagnosed atypical ulcer risks incontinence and delays a cancer or infection diagnosis.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden management item present in ios.radiation.plan: "if chronic / failed medical: lateral internal sphincterotomy"

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — management of anal fissures
guideline.section: Atypical fissures (lateral, multiple, painless, large, indurated): evaluate for Crohn’s disease, HIV, syphilis, tuberculosis, malignancy — EUA and biopsy
guideline.citation: Davids JS, Hawkins AT, Bhama AR, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anal fissures. Dis Colon Rectum. 2023;66:190–199.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — anal squamous cell cancers (revised 2018)
guideline.section: Biopsy suspicious anal lesions; people with HIV are at high risk of anal cancer
guideline.citation: Stewart DB, Gaertner WB, Glasgow SC, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for anal squamous cell cancers (revised 2018). Dis Colon Rectum. 2018;61:755–774.

rationale: Permutation: every "atypical" feature (lateral, painless, indurated, nodes) plus HIV. The plan must investigate, not treat as a fissure. Coded K60.2 (anal fissure, unspecified) because that is what the clinician would pick before the biopsy.
